title: Finite presentation of a closed immersion and finite type of its ideal
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Then $i$ is of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated) [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] if and only if $\mathcal I$ is of finite type as an $\mathcal O_X$-module, meaning that every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood on which finitely many sections generate $\mathcal I$. No Noetherian, quasi-compactness or separatedness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the Mathlib instances IsClosedImmersion -> IsAffineHom -> QuasiCompact and Mono -> QuasiSeparated. These give the two nonlocal finiteness conditions without assumptions on X.

The module realization of any ideal sheaf is quasi-coherent: it is the kernel of the structure sheaf map to the pushforward of the structure sheaf of its closed subscheme. The source and target are quasi-coherent by the unit instance and quasi-coherent pushforward along a closed immersion; apply closure under kernels.

For each affine open U, the section inclusion of i.ker.toModules is injective and has range i.ker.ideal U. Its range restriction is therefore a linear bijection. Module.Finite.iff_fg identifies finiteness of its section module with finite generation of this ideal. Scheme.Hom.ker_apply identifies this ideal with the kernel of i.app U.

For a surjective ring map f:R->S, finite presentation is equivalent to finite generation of its kernel. Forward: equip S with f.toAlgebra and apply Algebra.FinitePresentation.ker_fG_of_surjective to Algebra.ofId R S, using finite presentation of R over itself. This Mathlib strengthening of the polynomial-kernel lemma avoids the zero-variable polynomial equivalence. Reverse: use RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_surjective. Apply this to i.app U, surjective for affine U.

For the forward implication, local finite presentation gives finite presentation of i.app U because the full preimage of each affine open is affine. The preceding ring and section equivalences give finite section modules on the cover of all affine opens. Apply quasicoherent_finite_type_affine, clause (c), to conclude that i.ker.toModules is of finite type.

Conversely, finite type of the quasi-coherent kernel module gives finite section modules on every affine open by finite_sections_of_finiteType. The section and ring equivalences make each i.app U finitely presented. Around z choose an affine open U containing i(z), with affine inverse image. These witness HasRingHomProperty.iff_exists_appLE for local finite presentation. Combine with the instances from step 1.

The item statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged from the earlier dagsnap; the delivery adds only proof, proof_deps, split_report and logged searches. There are no new nodes and no re-split repair note. Step 1: a closed immersion is quasi-compact because the preimage of an affine open is affine (def-weil-closed-immersion, affine-scheme-qcqs, def-weil-finite-type-morphism). It is quasi-separated because 01QU(a) makes it separated, so its diagonal is a closed immersion and hence quasi-compact (def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism). No hypothesis on X is used. Step 2 is elementary: def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf states I(U)=J, I|_U=J~ and quasi-coherence explicitly. Step 3: R/J is finitely presented over R iff J is finitely generated, using the 00R2 node with n=0 and the 00F3 definition (n=0, m relations). Step 4: 01TQ on the affine pair (i^{-1}U, U), then step 3, then quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine (c) on an affine cover. Step 5: restrict to U, apply (a), then step 3, then use the affine pair (i^{-1}U, U) as the witness in def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation; together with step 1 this gives finite presentation. Each cited statement says what its step uses. The item's inline 'finite type' is the same notion as pqf-def-coherent (2). Small cases checked: J=0, J=R, empty X, a non-quasi-compact disjoint union of affines, and the non-f.g. ideal (x_1,x_2,...) in k[x_1,x_2,...].
